# Grouped line graphs {#sec-grp-line-graphs} ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="simple"} ## Theme: `theme_snick()` Graphs in this chapter use `fmggp2::theme_snick()`, built from Nickelodeon's Saturday night block (SNICK): a night purple background, a Nickelodeon orange frame and title, slime green, purple, blue, yellow, and pink marks, and an Arial Black title. ::: :::: {.callout-note collapse="false" icon=false}
::: {.cell layout-align="right"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](grp_line_graphs_files/figure-html/full_code_display-1.png){fig-align='right' width=60% height=60%} ::: ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #02577A;"} **Requirements:** ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"} **✅ a numeric (continuous) variable** ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"} **✅ a numeric (date) variable** ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"} **✅ at least one categorical variable** ::: :::: ## Description Grouped line graphs use color, line style, and faceting to show group changes over time for a continuous variable across categorical levels. ## Set up ::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"} **PACKAGES:** ::: Install packages. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} library(ggplot2) library(dplyr) # for tibble() and data manipulation library(lubridate) # for working with dates ``` ::: ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"} **DATA:** ::: Every Saturday night starting in 1992, Nickelodeon kids parked themselves in front of SNICK (*Clarissa Explains It All*, *Are You Afraid of the Dark?*, and *All That*) and the orange couch. We'll simulate a Nielsen style rating for Nickelodeon for every day from 1993 through 1999. Each night of the week gets its own average (`night_avg`), with Saturday on top. Two smooth patterns get added to the nightly averages: a `trend` that rises through the middle of the decade and falls off near the end, and a `summer` bump when school is out. Then `rnorm()` adds day to day noise. Setting the seed with `set.seed()` means you'll get the same 2,556 days every time you run the code below. We'll also create the date variables we need for grouping: - `day_of_week` (a factor from `wday()`, unordered so the graphs use the theme colors) and `day_category` (`"Weekday"` or `"Weekend"`) - `yr_mnth` (the first day of each month) and `yr_qtr` (the year and quarter) ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} set.seed(1992) nick_ratings <- tibble( date = seq(as.Date("1993-01-01"), as.Date("1999-12-31"), by = "day")) |> mutate( year = year(date), month = month(date), day_of_week = factor(wday(date, label = TRUE), ordered = FALSE), day_category = if_else(day_of_week %in% c("Sat", "Sun"), "Weekend", "Weekday"), yr_mnth = floor_date(date, unit = "month"), yr_qtr = factor(paste0(year, "/0", quarter(date)), ordered = TRUE), night_avg = c(Sun = 3.0, Mon = 2.4, Tue = 2.3, Wed = 2.3, Thu = 2.4, Fri = 2.8, Sat = 4.2)[as.character(day_of_week)], trend = 0.25 * (year - 1993) - 0.04 * (year - 1993)^2, summer = 0.3 * sin(2 * pi * (month - 4) / 12), rating = round(rnorm(n(), mean = night_avg + trend + summer, sd = 0.35), 2)) |> select(-night_avg, -trend, -summer) glimpse(nick_ratings) #> Rows: 2,556 #> Columns: 8 #> $ date 1993-01-01, 1993-01-02, 19… #> $ year 1993, 1993, 1993, 1993, 199… #> $ month 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, … #> $ day_of_week Fri, Sat, Sun, Mon, Tue, We… #> $ day_category "Weekday", "Weekend", "Week… #> $ yr_mnth 1993-01-01, 1993-01-01, 19… #> $ yr_qtr 1993/01, 1993/01, 1993/01, … #> $ rating 2.61, 4.20, 2.65, 1.81, 2.1… ``` ::: ::: We'll use these data in the *More info* section for more line graphs, but for now: - Group `nick_ratings` on `year` and `day_category` - Calculate the average `rating` as `avg_rating` - Store the data in `avg_rating_day_cat_yr`. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} avg_rating_day_cat_yr <- nick_ratings |> group_by(year, day_category) |> summarise(avg_rating = mean(rating)) |> ungroup() #> `summarise()` has regrouped the output. #> ℹ Summaries were computed grouped by year and #> day_category. #> ℹ Output is grouped by year. #> ℹ Use `summarise(.groups = "drop_last")` to #> silence this message. #> ℹ Use `summarise(.by = c(year, day_category))` #> for per-operation grouping (`?dplyr::dplyr_by`) #> instead. glimpse(avg_rating_day_cat_yr) #> Rows: 14 #> Columns: 3 #> $ year 1993, 1993, 1994, 1994, 199… #> $ day_category "Weekday", "Weekend", "Week… #> $ avg_rating 2.405057, 3.604519, 2.64930… ``` ::: ::: ## Distribution A grouped line graph rarely plots raw values. It plots an *average* for each group at each point in time, and averages behave very differently from the values they're built from. Below we'll move from the daily ratings, to a picture, to the formula, and see why averaging makes the group differences easy to see. ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **COUNT IT:** ::: Start with the first week of 1996. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} nick_ratings |> filter(year == 1996) |> select(date, day_of_week, rating) |> head(7) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ::: Saturday is the clear winner this week, but the weeknights are close enough that the order could flip next week. Below we count every night in 1996 and calculate the mean and standard deviation for each night of the week. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} nick_1996 <- nick_ratings |> filter(year == 1996) |> group_by(day_of_week) |> summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(rating), sd = sd(rating)) nick_1996 ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ::: Each night of the week shows up 52 or 53 times in a year. The Saturday mean (4.63) is well above the Tuesday mean (2.67), but any single night wanders about 0.4 rating points from its mean. ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **DRAW IT:** ::: The graph below draws every Tuesday and Saturday rating from 1996 as a thin, faded line, then adds each month's average as a thick line. The daily lines zig and zag, while the monthly averages are much smoother. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} tue_sat_1996 <- nick_ratings |> filter(year == 1996, day_of_week %in% c("Tue", "Sat")) tue_sat_monthly <- tue_sat_1996 |> group_by(yr_mnth, day_of_week) |> summarise(avg_rating = mean(rating), .groups = "drop") ggplot() + geom_line(data = tue_sat_1996, aes(x = date, y = rating, color = day_of_week), alpha = 1 / 3) + geom_line(data = tue_sat_monthly, aes(x = yr_mnth, y = avg_rating, color = day_of_week), linewidth = 1.5) + labs(x = "1996", y = "Rating", color = "Night") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](grp_line_graphs_files/figure-html/draw_grp_line-1.png){width=576} ::: ::: ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **NAME IT:** ::: Each day's rating is a draw from a [normal distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_distribution) centered on that night's average for that time of year: $$ \text{rating}_d \sim \text{Normal}\left(\mu_{\text{night}} + \text{trend}_{\text{year}} + \text{summer}_{\text{month}}, \; \sigma = 0.35\right) $$ The standard deviation of an average of $n$ draws is $\sigma / \sqrt{n}$ (the [standard error](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_error)). A monthly average of about four Saturdays wobbles by about $0.35 / \sqrt{4} \approx 0.18$ points, and a yearly average of about 52 Saturdays wobbles by only $0.35 / \sqrt{52} \approx 0.05$ points. That's why the yearly `avg_rating` lines below are so smooth, and why the gap between weekdays and weekends stands out. The `sd` column in **COUNT IT** is a little larger than 0.35 because it also includes the summer bump. Try changing `sd = 0.35` to `sd = 1` and watch the daily lines in **DRAW IT** turn into a tangle while the yearly lines barely move. ## Grammar ::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"} **CODE:** ::: - Create labels with `labs()` - Map `year` to the `x`, `avg_rating` to the `y`, and `day_category` to `group` - Add the `geom_line()` layer and map `day_category` to color (*inside* `aes()`) ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} labs_line_graph <- labs(title = "Nickelodeon ratings", caption = "Simulated data", subtitle = "1993-1999", y = "Average rating", x = "Year", color = "Day Category") ggp2_line <- ggplot(data = avg_rating_day_cat_yr, mapping = aes(x = year, y = avg_rating, group = day_category)) + geom_line(aes(color = day_category)) ggp2_line + labs_line_graph ``` ::: ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"} **GRAPH:** ::: ::: {.cell layout-nrow="1"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](grp_line_graphs_files/figure-html/create_graph_line-1.png){width=100% height=100%} ::: ::: ## More info Line graphs are great for displaying relationships across variables with multiple groups (or levels). We can also use facets for multiple comparisons (i.e., small multiples). ### Groups In the previous graph, we can see the ratings peak around `1996` or `1997`. - We'll create another summarized dataset from `nick_ratings`, but this time we restrict the observations to the ratings between `1996` and `1997` - Group the data on `yr_qtr` and `day_of_week` - Then calculate the average `rating` as `avg_rating` ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} avg_rating_dow_qtr <- nick_ratings |> filter(year >= 1996 & year <= 1997) |> group_by(yr_qtr, day_of_week) |> summarise(avg_rating = mean(rating)) |> ungroup() glimpse(avg_rating_dow_qtr) #> Rows: 56 #> Columns: 3 #> $ yr_qtr 1996/01, 1996/01, 1996/01, 1… #> $ day_of_week Sun, Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri… #> $ avg_rating 2.941538, 2.486923, 2.319231… ``` ::: ::: Now when we create our line graph, we will have a categorical variable with seven levels (`day_of_week`): + Create subtitle using `paste0()` to ensure it's accurate if/when the underlying data is updated. + Move the legend to the top of the graph using `theme(legend.position = "top")` (to improve readability). ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} # here we create the labels (with the subtitle updating with the data) labs_line_graph_grp <- labs(title = "Nickelodeon ratings", caption = "Simulated data", subtitle = paste0("Between ", min(avg_rating_dow_qtr$yr_qtr), " and ", max(avg_rating_dow_qtr$yr_qtr)), y = "Average rating", x = "Year/Quarter", color = "Day of Week") ``` ::: ::: ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} # Build layer with yr_qtr and day_of_week ggp2_line_grp <- ggplot(data = avg_rating_dow_qtr, mapping = aes(x = yr_qtr, y = avg_rating, group = day_of_week)) + geom_line(aes(color = day_of_week)) # move legend ggp2_line_grp + labs_line_graph_grp + theme(legend.position = "top") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](grp_line_graphs_files/figure-html/ggp2_line_grp-1.png){width=576} ::: ::: ::: The Saturday line sits on top of every quarter (that's SNICK), and every night rises and falls with the summer bump. ### Line Styles - We can make it easier to distinguish between lines in our graph by adjusting the line style (`linetype` and `linewidth`), or by changing overall opacity (`alpha`). - We'll work through some examples below using another subset from `nick_ratings`. ::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"} **DATA:** ::: ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} avg_rating_dow_mnth <- nick_ratings |> filter(year >= 1996 & year <= 1997) |> group_by(yr_mnth, day_of_week) |> summarise(avg_rating = mean(rating)) |> ungroup() glimpse(avg_rating_dow_mnth) #> Rows: 168 #> Columns: 3 #> $ yr_mnth 1996-01-01, 1996-01-01, 199… #> $ day_of_week Sun, Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri… #> $ avg_rating 3.0575, 2.5040, 2.2940, 2.39… ``` ::: ::: ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} labs_line_styles <- labs( title = "Nickelodeon ratings", caption = "Simulated data", subtitle = paste0( "Between ", min(avg_rating_dow_mnth$yr_mnth), " and ", max(avg_rating_dow_mnth$yr_mnth) ), y = "Average rating", x = "Year-Month", color = "Day of Week" ) ``` ::: ::: ### `alpha` & `linewidth` Line styles are an excellent tool for highlighting or emphasizing certain lines over others. - We'll start by creating a line graph layer for Monday (`"Mon"`), Thursday (`"Thu"`), and Friday (`"Fri"`) adjusting the opacity with `alpha`. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} ggp2_line_mon_thu_fri <- ggplot(data = filter(avg_rating_dow_mnth, day_of_week %in% c("Mon", "Thu", "Fri"))) + geom_line( aes(x = yr_mnth, y = avg_rating, group = day_of_week, color = day_of_week), alpha = 1 / 4, linewidth = 0.85) # layer 1 ggp2_line_mon_thu_fri + labs_line_styles + theme(legend.position = "top") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](grp_line_graphs_files/figure-html/ggp2_line_mon_thu_fri-1.png){width=576} ::: ::: ::: ### `linetype` Then we'll change the `linetype` of Saturday and Sunday to `"longdash"` (and make this *somewhat* transparent with a slightly higher `alpha`). ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} ggp2_line_sat_sun <- ggp2_line_mon_thu_fri + geom_line(data = filter(avg_rating_dow_mnth, day_of_week %in% c("Sat", "Sun")), aes(x = yr_mnth, y = avg_rating, group = day_of_week, color = day_of_week), alpha = 1 / 2, linewidth = 0.75, linetype = "longdash") # layers 1 & 2 ggp2_line_sat_sun + labs_line_styles + theme(legend.position = "top") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](grp_line_graphs_files/figure-html/ggp2_line_sat_sun-1.png){width=576} ::: ::: ::: ### Color palettes - Add `geom_line()` for Tuesday and Wednesday, and set the colors manually with `scale_color_manual()` (below we use a named vector of SNICK colors). - We also manually set the legend order by supplying the original factor levels to the `breaks` argument. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} # original factor levels lev_order <- levels(avg_rating_dow_mnth$day_of_week) # SNICK colors snick_pal <- c(Sun = "#FF5FA2", Mon = "#29B6F6", Tue = "#8CC63F", Wed = "#FFD200", Thu = "#B07CE8", Fri = "#F4F1FA", Sat = "#F57D0D") # layer 3 ggp2_line_pal_d <- ggp2_line_sat_sun + # add line geom_line(data = filter(avg_rating_dow_mnth, day_of_week %in% c("Tue", "Wed")), aes(x = yr_mnth, y = avg_rating, group = day_of_week, color = day_of_week), linewidth = 1.25) + # add palette scale_color_manual( breaks = lev_order, # original factor levels values = snick_pal) # three layers ggp2_line_pal_d + # labels labs_line_styles + # legend position theme(legend.position = "top") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](grp_line_graphs_files/figure-html/ggp2_line_pal_d-1.png){width=576} ::: ::: ::: Changing the look of the lines is a great way to highlight or emphasize some lines over others. ### Labels We'll use labels to display the highest daily rating and the highest monthly average rating for a few nights of the week. - To accomplish this, we're going to create two small tables of labels, `label_max_dow` and `label_max_avg_dow`, that we'll use to label the maximum values. - Each has a row for every night of the week (`label_max_dow` can have more if two nights tie for the max) and a label variable (`lbl`) which we can use with `geom_label()`. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} label_max_dow <- nick_ratings |> group_by(day_of_week) |> summarise(max_rating = max(rating)) |> ungroup() |> inner_join(y = nick_ratings, by = c("max_rating" = "rating", "day_of_week")) |> mutate(lbl = paste0(day_of_week, " (", date, "), max rating = ", max_rating)) |> select(day_of_week, yr_mnth, max_rating, lbl) arrange(label_max_dow, desc(max_rating)) |> slice(1:2) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ::: ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} label_max_avg_dow <- avg_rating_dow_mnth |> # group by sun-sat group_by(day_of_week) |> # get max avg slice_max(order_by = avg_rating, n = 1) |> # ungroup ungroup() |> rename(max_avg_rating = avg_rating) |> mutate(lbl = paste0(day_of_week, ": max avg rating = ", round(max_avg_rating, 2))) arrange(label_max_avg_dow, desc(max_avg_rating)) |> slice(1:2) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ::: Now that we have label tables for each metric, we can filter them to the days we want to label. - We'll use `filter()` to get the maximum values for `"Wed"` (in `label_max_wed_dow` and `label_max_avg_wed_dow`) ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} # get wed label_max_wed_dow <- label_max_dow |> filter(day_of_week == "Wed") label_max_wed_dow ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} label_max_avg_wed_dow <- label_max_avg_dow |> filter(day_of_week == "Wed") label_max_avg_wed_dow ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ::: Add `geom_point()` and `geom_label()` for Wednesday. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} # point for max rating ggp2_line_wed_max_pnts <- geom_point( data = label_max_wed_dow, aes(x = yr_mnth, y = max_rating, color = day_of_week), size = 2.5, show.legend = FALSE) ggp2_line_wed_max_avg_pnts <- geom_point( data = label_max_avg_wed_dow, aes(x = yr_mnth, y = max_avg_rating, color = day_of_week), size = 2.5, alpha = 1/2, show.legend = FALSE) ggp2_line_wed_max_lbl <- geom_label( data = label_max_wed_dow, aes(x = yr_mnth, y = max_rating, label = lbl, color = day_of_week), fill = "#1E1238", nudge_y = 0.25, nudge_x = 60, size = 2.5, show.legend = FALSE) ggp2_line_wed_max_avg_lbl <- geom_label(data = label_max_avg_wed_dow, aes(x = yr_mnth, y = max_avg_rating, label = lbl, color = day_of_week), fill = "#1E1238", nudge_y = -0.35, nudge_x = 60, size = 2.5, show.legend = FALSE) ggp2_line_pal_d + ggp2_line_wed_max_pnts + ggp2_line_wed_max_avg_pnts + ggp2_line_wed_max_lbl + ggp2_line_wed_max_avg_lbl + # add labels labs_line_styles + # move legend to top theme(legend.position = "top") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](grp_line_graphs_files/figure-html/ggp2_line_wed_labels-1.png){width=576} ::: ::: ::: We'll use `filter()` to get the maximum values for `"Tue"` (in `label_max_tue_dow` and `label_max_avg_tue_dow`): ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} # get tue label_max_tue_dow <- label_max_dow |> filter(day_of_week == "Tue") label_max_tue_dow ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} label_max_avg_tue_dow <- label_max_avg_dow |> filter(day_of_week == "Tue") label_max_avg_tue_dow ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ::: Add `geom_point()` and `geom_label()` for Tuesday ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} # point for max rating ggp2_line_tue_max_pnts <- geom_point(data = label_max_tue_dow, aes(x = yr_mnth, y = max_rating, color = day_of_week), size = 2.5, show.legend = FALSE) ggp2_line_tue_max_avg_pnts <- geom_point( data = label_max_avg_tue_dow, aes(x = yr_mnth, y = max_avg_rating, color = day_of_week), size = 2.5, alpha = 1/2, show.legend = FALSE) ggp2_line_tue_max_lbl <- geom_label(data = label_max_tue_dow, aes(x = yr_mnth, y = max_rating, label = lbl, color = day_of_week), fill = "#1E1238", nudge_y = 0.25, nudge_x = -60, size = 2.5, show.legend = FALSE) ggp2_line_tue_max_avg_lbl <- geom_label(data = label_max_avg_tue_dow, aes(x = yr_mnth, y = max_avg_rating, label = lbl, color = day_of_week), fill = "#1E1238", nudge_y = -0.35, nudge_x = -60, size = 2.5, show.legend = FALSE) ggp2_line_pal_d + # wednesday layers ggp2_line_wed_max_pnts + ggp2_line_wed_max_avg_pnts + ggp2_line_wed_max_lbl + ggp2_line_wed_max_avg_lbl + # tuesday layers ggp2_line_tue_max_pnts + ggp2_line_tue_max_avg_pnts + ggp2_line_tue_max_lbl + ggp2_line_tue_max_avg_lbl + # add labels labs_line_styles + # move legend to top theme(legend.position = "top") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](grp_line_graphs_files/figure-html/ggp2_line_tue_labels-1.png){width=576} ::: ::: ::: Notice the highest daily ratings sit well above the highest monthly averages. A single night can get lucky, but an average of four nights rarely does (just like we saw in the **Distribution** section). ### Facets Finally, we can use facets to view each of the line graphs separately (or small multiples). - We'll create a dataset with the daily ratings between `1998-07-01` and `1999-12-31` and store it as `daily_ratings_9899` ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} daily_ratings_9899 <- nick_ratings |> filter(date >= as.Date("1998-07-01")) |> select(date, day_category, day_of_week, rating) glimpse(daily_ratings_9899) #> Rows: 549 #> Columns: 4 #> $ date 1998-07-01, 1998-07-02, 19… #> $ day_category "Weekday", "Weekday", "Week… #> $ day_of_week Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun, Mo… #> $ rating 3.11, 2.48, 3.68, 4.25, 3.3… ``` ::: ::: - Using `facet_wrap()` with a single categorical variable (`. ~ var`) will create a plot for each discrete level, while `facet_grid()` will create a level-by-level grid (specified as `var ~ var`). ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} # labels labs_line_graph_facet_wrap <- labs( title = "Nickelodeon ratings", caption = "Simulated data", subtitle = paste0( "Between ", min(daily_ratings_9899$date), " and ", max(daily_ratings_9899$date) ), y = "Rating", x = "Date", color = "Day of Week" ) # layer ggp2_line_facet_wrap <- ggplot(data = daily_ratings_9899, mapping = aes(x = date, y = rating, group = day_of_week)) + geom_line(aes(color = day_of_week)) + scale_color_manual(values = snick_pal) + scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(2, 3, 4, 5)) + scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y") + facet_wrap(day_of_week ~ ., shrink = TRUE) ggp2_line_facet_wrap + labs_line_graph_facet_wrap + theme(legend.position = "top") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](grp_line_graphs_files/figure-html/ggp2_line_facet_wrap-1.png){width=576} ::: ::: ::: - It's always a good idea to check the `x` and `y` axis text when using facets. I've adjusted the `x` and `y` axes above using `scale_y_continuous()` and `scale_x_date()` before adding `facet_wrap()` ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} # labels labs_line_graph_facet_grid <- labs( title = "Nickelodeon ratings", caption = "Simulated data", subtitle = paste0( "Between ", min(daily_ratings_9899$date), " and ", max(daily_ratings_9899$date) ), y = "Rating", x = "Date", color = "Day of Week" ) # layer ggp2_line_facet_grid <- ggplot(data = daily_ratings_9899, mapping = aes(x = date, y = rating, group = day_of_week)) + geom_line(aes(color = day_of_week)) + scale_color_manual(values = snick_pal) + scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(2, 3, 4, 5)) + scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y") + facet_grid(day_of_week ~ day_category, shrink = TRUE) ggp2_line_facet_grid + labs_line_graph_facet_grid ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](grp_line_graphs_files/figure-html/ggp2_line_facet_grid-1.png){width=576} ::: ::: ::: The colors have been set manually using `scale_color_manual()` and the `snick_pal` named vector we created in the *Color palettes* section.
